item.title: OJK Boss Mahendra Siregar Steps Down
item.description: Jakarta. Mahendra Siregar, who has been helming the Financial Services Authority or OJK for over 3 years, officially stepped down on Friday following market turmoil. Mahendra was not alone. Inarno Djajadi — the OJK’s chief executive for capital market, financial derivative, and carbon exchange supervision — has also quit. The same goes for I. B. item.title: Police Find No Foul Play in Death of Influencer Lula Lahfah
item.description: Jakarta. Police have halted their investigation into the death of social media influencer Lula Lahfah, who was found dead in her apartment unit last week, after concluding there were no indications of a criminal act. item.title: Indonesia’s Market Meltdown Claims Its Regulators
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s financial regulators staged an extraordinary collective retreat on Friday, resigning in rapid succession after a sharp market sell-off rattled investor confidence and exposed long-standing weaknesses in market governance. item.title: Nearly $900 Billion Wiped Off Indonesia’s Stock Market in Turbulent Week
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s benchmark stock index suffered one of its most volatile weeks in recent years in late January, prompting the resignation of senior leaders at both the country’s financial regulator and stock exchange as authorities grappled with a sharp market sell-off linked to global index policy changes. item.title: Gold Prices Slide Sharply as Fed Signals and Equity Rebound Sap Safe-Haven Demand
item.description: Jakarta. International and domestic gold prices fell sharply at the end of January as shifting expectations around the US Federal Reserve and a rebound in equity markets prompted investors to rotate out of safe-haven assets. Spot gold plunged 8.15% to $4,893.20 (Rp 82,076,090) per ounce on Saturday, while silver suffered an even steeper drop, sliding 25.5% to $85.34 per ounce. item.title: Who Is Kevin Warsh, Trump’s Pick to Lead the Federal Reserve?
item.description: Washington. President Donald Trump says he will nominate former Federal Reserve governor Kevin Warsh to replace Jerome Powell as chair of the US central bank when Powell’s term ends in May, betting that Warsh can deliver the stronger growth Trump promised voters.
